chief_complaint: excessive, uncontrollable worry about everyday routines and muscle tension for 6 months
hpi_details: 34F reports 6 months of constant, excessive worry regarding her health, finances, and children's safety. Describes feeling restless, easily fatigued, having neck muscle tension, and sleep onset insomnia.
ideas: She thinks she might have a thyroid problem or severe burnout from trying to balance a demanding office job with raising her children.
concerns: worried about panic attacks or needing nerve pills

clinical_knowledge.topic: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) evaluation and management
core_concepts: GAD is excessive, difficult-to-control worry across several domains for at least 6 months with associated symptoms and impairment.
Assess impairment, panic, depression, mania, substance use, medicines, trauma, and medical contributors such as thyroid disease when indicated.
CBT and other structured psychological therapies are first-line options; discuss medication only after individualized assessment and shared decision-making.
Benzodiazepines are not routine long-term treatment because of dependence, sedation, and withdrawal risks.

Key HPI features: 34F reports 6 months of constant, excessive worry regarding her health, finances, and children's safety. Describes feeling restless, easily fatigued, having neck muscle tension, and sleep onset insomnia.
Objective/Exam findings: Mental-state examination, vital signs, medication and substance review, and targeted tests only if suggested by history or examination.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Adjustment disorder without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Acute suicidal or homicidal ideation.
management_principles: Assess safety, severity, functional impairment, and medical or substance-related causes; a GAD-7 can support but not replace clinical assessment.
Offer CBT and discuss SSRI or SNRI treatment when appropriate, including adverse effects, interactions, early activation, and follow-up.
Urgently assess and escalate for suicidal intent, psychosis, mania, severe self-neglect, or inability to remain safe.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

must_ask.say: Do you worry excessively about your health, finances, or your children's safety, more days than not?
Is it difficult for you to control the worry once it starts?
Do you feel restless, tense in your neck, or easily fatigued?
Does the worry make it hard for you to fall asleep?
Do you have episodes of sudden intense fear, or feel depressed?

history.answer: I've been feeling constantly anxious and worried about everything for the past six months, and my neck is always stiff.
I worry constantly about my health, our family finances, and whether something bad might happen to my kids.
It started about six months ago without any single trigger, and it has been present almost every single day.
It feels like a steady hum of worry throughout the day rather than coming and going in brief waves.
I try so hard to push the thoughts away, but I just cannot seem to stop or control them.
No, I haven't had sudden attacks of a racing heart, choking sensations, or feeling like I am about to die.
I don't avoid crowded places or leave the house in fear; I just carry my worries everywhere I go.
No, speaking in front of people or being judged isn't what makes me anxious.
My neck and shoulders are constantly tense and sore, and I feel keyed up and unable to sit still.
I tire out very quickly during the day, and my mind constantly goes blank when I try to focus at work.
It takes me more than an hour to fall asleep each night because my mind keeps racing with worries.
It slows me down at my office job, and by the time I get home, I'm too exhausted to enjoy time with my children.
There haven't been any sudden disasters, but managing normal work deadlines and household bills feels completely overwhelming.
No, I haven't experienced any traumatic events, and I don't have nightmares or flashbacks.
I don't have urges to wash my hands repeatedly or check door locks over and over.
I don't feel hopeless or sad all day, just worn out and frustrated by how anxious I am.
No, I have never thought about ending my life or hurting myself. I want to get better for my family.
No, my weight has been completely steady, and I don't feel unusually hot or sweaty.
No, I've never had chest pain when exercising, and I have never passed out.
I only drink one mug of brewed coffee in the morning and no energy drinks.
I don't use any recreational drugs, and I've never taken sleeping pills or nerve medicines.
I've tried deep breathing exercises and drinking chamomile tea before bed, but they barely help.
I've been wondering if my thyroid is acting up or if I'm just completely burned out from trying to manage my office job and the kids.
I'm terrified this might escalate into full-blown panic attacks, or that I'll be forced to take addictive nerve pills.
I'm hoping to learn cognitive behavioral therapy techniques and discuss safe medication options to help calm my nerves.
I have mild irritable bowel syndrome that flares up when I'm stressed, but nothing else.
I have never had any surgeries or been admitted to a hospital.
I don't take any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, or herbal supplements right now.
I don't have any known allergies to medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used electronic vapes.
I only have an occasional glass of wine at a dinner party, perhaps once a month.
I work as an office administrator and live with my husband and two elementary-school-aged children.
My mother has always been a very nervous and anxious person, but no one in my family has bipolar disorder or psychosis.
My periods are regular every twenty-eight days, my last one was two weeks ago, and we use condoms so there's no chance of pregnancy.
